claim: Moldova runs several front ends whose relationship the sources do not state, so it offers no tested single-portal model.
problem: Claim of absence contradicted. The observatory factsheet lists the Public Service Portal as a module of EVO and MCabinet as another module, and calls the business portal an extension of MCabinet. The agency calls EVO the single government portal and plans to centralise all access under it. The pass 2 note on item 0014 reads 'link between EVO and the portal'. None of these except 0005 is used in the case. The comparator relevance reason repeats 'several front ends instead of one portal'.
suggested_fix: State the relationship: EVO is described as a modular front end over the portal, and the agency's single-portal claim is unverified and recent. The conclusion that no single-portal model has been tested can stay if it rests on the absence of use data, not on silence about the relationship. Amend the CMP-0007 relevance reason to match.

claim: adopted: 'no item assesses the strategy's delivery as such'.
problem: Claim of absence contradicted, and the value does not follow. The Commission says the government 'continued to implement' the strategy with 'notable progress' on all key performance indicators, and pass 2 links item 0002 to INT-MDA-0007. An equivalent Commission statement sets INT-ALB-0004 to implemented, so the two countries are treated differently. The judgement cites only the 2023 brief.
suggested_fix: Cite both Commission items and propose implemented, noting that the wording is chapter-wide and that the 75% target for end-2024 stands against 70% reported in 2026.

claim: 'no source traces what institutions did to the law, and the one duty traced to practice, e-payment, is reported as limited'.
problem: Claim of absence contradicted. The monitor traces a second duty under the same law to practice: the once-only rule is 'explicitly mandated' by the law and 'generally has been effectively implemented', and pass 2 links this item to INT-ALB-0006. It conflicts with the monitor's own survey (half of citizens still asked; score 0.5 of 2), which the extraction note already records. The judgement cites neither side.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the reason to report both duties and cite both sides of the once-only conflict. Reconsider the value at the gate, since the law is traced to practice in part; adopted may still stand but not on the stated ground. Check the CMP-0008 phrase on the legal duty for the same omission.

claim: 'No item assesses delivery of the strategy itself.'
problem: Claim of absence contradicted. Item MNE-GOV-2025-002-0007 comes from the ministry's report on the strategy's action plan and gives 43.14% of planned 2024 activities fulfilled; the extraction note says it refers to all strategy activities. The monitor repeats the figure at page 7 of its report. The figure also appears nowhere in CMP-0009.
suggested_fix: Cite the item and propose implemented (partly delivered on the ministry's own report), or keep adopted with the reason corrected. Add the 43.14% to how_implemented in CMP-0009, labelled as government reporting and machine translated.

claim: mixed
problem: The value does not follow from the reason or from the case. CMP-0008 says the indicator 'counts any online contact with authorities, not portal use', so the figure does not measure a result of this portal. The other evidence in the reason concerns payment and access, not this outcome. Sibling outcomes from the same source are insufficient_evidence, and the source is the only one for the use figures.
suggested_fix: Propose insufficient_evidence, in line with the sibling rows, and say that the broad indicator cannot show a result of the portal.

claim: Medium: 'The count belongs to the portal as a channel, but no source says what caused the growth.'
problem: The value does not follow from the reason. The outcome is growth from 15.2 to 17 million, and the reason says nothing shows why it grew. The figures have no stated origin and success on the same link is insufficient_evidence. CMP-0008 lists portal consolidation, the law, closed counters and pre-filled forms as inseparable. Comparable Moldovan rows are Low.
suggested_fix: Propose Low. The channel point can stay in the reason as a statement about where the count is taken.

claim: implemented
problem: The value does not follow. The reason itself reports a conflict, rests on self-reporting and notes no confirmation that the services are transactional. The plan runs to 2027 and covers 171 services, so 57 is one yearly tranche, and the plan was revised in December 2025. INT-ALB-0008, also in progress, is set at adopted. A conflict between sources is tier 3 and the value silently takes the government's side.
suggested_fix: Propose unclear, or adopted with delivery under way, and flag it as a conflict for the analyst. Say that 57 is the 2025 tranche of 171.

claim: 'Concentrating responsibility in one body answers North Macedonia's fragmented ownership, and the monitor states that this resolved institutional overlaps in Albania.'
problem: Goes further than the evidence. In the source table (monitor page 36) the overlap is a narrow one: monitoring, evaluation and reporting between ADISA and the Agency for Dialogue and Co-governance. It says nothing about ownership of digitalisation across government. North Macedonia's problem also differs: MISA already leads and lacks resources and cooperation, so naming one body does not answer it. The sentence has no measure behind it, and informants report ADISA's effectiveness declining. The worked row and can_be_attributed do not state how narrow the overlap is.
suggested_fix: Limit the lesson to removing one named overlap between two bodies. Remove 'answers'. Say that North Macedonia already has a lead ministry. State the narrow overlap in the worked reason and in can_be_attributed.

claim: 'the independent monitor closes during 2025'; 'measured within months of the first services in April 2025'.
problem: Wrong date basis. The report says its findings run to the end of 2024 and that during the monitoring period the portal was under construction (report pages 6 and 34; item metadata gives second half of 2022 to end of 2024). Later events are notes made at the time of writing. So the grades were set before the portal had any services, and the null result is partly timing. too_early survives, but its stated ground is wrong. The cause the monitor gives (sampled services not on the portal) is not the only explanation available.
suggested_fix: Correct both passages: findings to the end of 2024, portal under construction then, later notes to July 2025. Extract the 'under construction' sentence (page 34) as an item, and say in the reason that the grades largely predate the first services.

claim: 'it is a stalled case so far'; the lesson on launching a portal; 'The underlying mechanism applies directly: a portal adds little where the services people need sit elsewhere'.
problem: Goes further than the evidence. Given the monitoring period above, the null result largely predates the portal, the portal is judged too_early in this same file, and no item measures use of eUprava. 'Stalled' also conflicts with the too_early value and rests on sources that stop before most reported delivery; the government's later figures are untested, not refuted. 'Adds little' generalises from one monitor and seven sampled services, and that monitor also reports a gain in information. No transferability judgement covers this lesson.
suggested_fix: Replace 'stalled' with 'too early and unverified'. Replace 'applies directly' with a conditional wording. Say that the lesson is a hypothesis drawn from a sample taken before the first services. Add a transferability row on a lesson item, or mark the lesson as the agent's own and not a stated lesson.

claim: 'the government states 45 transactional services now, while the monitor finds none at level 5, and the two are not reconciled'; 'the monitor finds no service at level 5'.
problem: Attribution blurred. The monitor's passage reports the state of play in the government's own Digital Services Plan 2025-2027 (report pages 33 to 34). It is not an independent test, and it predates the delivery reported later. problem_addressed says 'citing the government's own plan', but evidence_of_results and the judgement reason use it as the monitor's finding against government reporting. The conflict is therefore between two government statements at different dates, and there is no independent count of transactional services at all.
suggested_fix: Attribute the level 5 statement to the plan as cited by the monitor, give its date basis, and say that no independent source counts transactional services. Correct the success reason, which uses it as outside evidence.

claim: Figures from machine-translated Montenegrin and Romanian government and audit reports (106 services, 25 and 57 of 57, two officials, the budget refusal, 'key challenges', the Court of Accounts statement).
problem: Outside the limit as worded. LIM-0029 allows machine-translated comparator 'legal texts' only; LIM-0012 covers Macedonian and Albanian only. These sources are government reports and an audit report, not legal texts. G2b passed them without row review, subject to confirmation at G6b. The CMP-0009 limitations never say that these figures are machine translated and capped at Medium, and item MNE-GOV-2025-002-0008 is also flagged possible_misread.
suggested_fix: Raise at G6b as an analyst decision: extend LIM-0029 to government reports, or drop these items. Add the machine-translation caveat to the CMP-0009 limitations either way.

claim: 'Every use figure after 2023 comes from the agency, a survey it commissioned or the project's funder.'
problem: Contradicted. The observatory factsheet gives 'only 20% of requests' at counters for businesses in June 2024, with no source (the INT-MDA-0002 reason says so), and the Commission gives e-signature users of 200,000 and over 266,000. The conclusion that no independent check exists can stand for portal use.
suggested_fix: Reword to say that figures on online requests and access come from those sources or have no stated source, and that the Commission's e-signature figures measure signature use only.

claim: 'Counting use service by service, and separating fully from partly digital services, does not depend on Moldova's context and would address North Macedonia's conflicting service counts.'
problem: Goes further than the evidence. The case itself says the 2022 count has not been repeated, and Moldova still has conflicting counts (283, 303 of 648, 445 of 636). Nothing shows the practice resolved conflicts in Moldova. 'Does not depend on context' is asserted without an item, and no transferability row covers it.
suggested_fix: Reword: a one-off count showed the gap in Moldova, and it could help in North Macedonia if repeated; Moldova has not shown it settles conflicting counts.

claim: 'a barrier also planned for in North Macedonia's DigInfo centres'.
problem: Overstated. The strategy commits only to 'an analysis for establishing' the centres, or upgrading one-stop-shop centres. The item ID is not cited in the case.
suggested_fix: Say that North Macedonia plans an analysis for such centres, and cite the item.

claim: High: 'the same mechanism as North Macedonia (MEC-11) with the only service-level use data in the three cases'.
problem: Rests on 2022 data and leaves out later evidence. The agency reports 71% of requests online, the Commission says use 'significantly increased', and CMP-0008 is held to Medium because reported use is high. 'Only service-level use data' also overlooks an out-of-scope Montenegrin figure for online enrolment, though that one is a single service.
suggested_fix: Add the later reported rise to the reason and say why the Commission's low-demand finding still supports the match, or reconsider against the Albanian rating.

claim: '292,179 users and 2,070 monthly applications in 2024'.
problem: The source gives no reference period ('currently'), as the extraction note records. 2024 is the report year. The item is cited in judgements but not in the case.
suggested_fix: Say 'in the Commission's 2024 report' and cite the item. List the other North Macedonian items used in the cases too (for example MKD-GOV-2024-007-0055 and 0136, MKD-GOV-2025-004-0194, MKD-GOV-2023-002-0021).

claim: MSign stays at implemented, with only an update, the audit mention and the brief's barrier cited.
problem: Evidence left out. The Commission says e-signature use 'is active' with 200,000 and over 266,000 users. The item does not name MSign, but the reason should say why it does not bear on the status.
suggested_fix: Mention the figures and state that they are not tied to MSign.

claim: 'Albania's gap is depth and inclusion more than range'; 'a contrast case for range'.
problem: Conflicting evidence not reported. The same RCC source says Albania 'continues to lag behind the regional average in certain aspects of service scope and sophistication', with a citizen services score of 50 against 53. The item is not cited.
suggested_fix: Report the RCC's statement alongside the 95% figures and record the conflict.

claim: 'no source shows that the duty caused either'; transactions 'not established'.
problem: Conflict not reported. The monitor states that 'these reforms explain why' informants describe 'transactional reliability' and ease of access. The extraction note calls this the only causal statement in the report; it concerns informants' views, not use. It also sits against the footnote that payment 'usually does not work'. The absence claims hold narrowly, but this item should be shown.
suggested_fix: Add the statement to the limitations, with the conflict and its three-informant base.

claim: 'A legal duty on institutions to integrate services could address range'.
problem: Sits against the case's own finding that no source shows the duty caused the range, and the Albanian law is not shown to have done so. The same field gives no evidence for it beyond coexistence.
suggested_fix: Reword as an untested option, or move it to the limits of the lesson.

claim: 'proposes updating the law towards mandatory integration of each e-service on the portal'.
problem: The item says 'mandatory integration or connection', and it is a machine-translated proposal. Leaving out 'or connection' makes it look closer to the Albanian single-channel duty than it is. The item is not cited.
suggested_fix: Add 'or connection' and cite the item.

claim: The e-government user indicator 'counts any online contact with authorities'; informant scores are points 'awarded only if all informants agree'.
problem: Both are correct against the source text (RCC report introduction to the indicator; monitor methodology, pages 38 to 39) but no evidence item holds them, so they cannot be traced under the quoting rule.
suggested_fix: Extract both passages as items.

claim: in_practice: 'The RCC's statement gives no measure of use.'
problem: Threshold applied unevenly. INT-MNE-0020, INT-MNE-0021 and INT-MDA-0015 stop at implemented because no use is measured. The reason also leaves out that half of surveyed citizens are still asked for documents the state holds.
suggested_fix: Propose implemented, or say what evidence of operation meets in_practice, and apply it to all three countries.

claim: reversed: 'this is supersession, not abandonment'.
problem: The reason argues against its own value. Reversed in the extraction rules means repealed, suspended or withdrawn. Pass 2 on item 0013 also does not link this intervention.
suggested_fix: Choose unclear or hold ADISA only as an actor, as the reason suggests; do not leave reversed standing with a reason that rejects it.

claim: Medium: 'that shows where they passed, not why people used it'.
problem: Weak fit. The reason states a tautology about the channel, not a contribution to the outcome, and the figures have no stated origin. It sits beside success at insufficient_evidence.
suggested_fix: Propose Low, or say explicitly that Medium applies to the channel only and not to the volume.

claim: 'An order set up the work'.
problem: The order (Prime Minister's Order No. 72 of 9 June 2023) is in the monitor's text at page 27 and in the entity row, but neither cited item contains it.
suggested_fix: Extract the sentence as an item and cite it.

claim: The case gives a practical lesson and transferable claims, but no transferability row.
problem: No item from the Albanian evidence is typed as a lesson, so no lesson has been judged. The case-level lesson is the agent's own synthesis. ALB-CSO-2025-001-0072 and ALB-CSO-2025-001-0006 come closest.
suggested_fix: Say in the case that the lesson is the agent's synthesis, or retype one item at the gate and judge it.

claim: 'a plan for transactional services 2025-2027 covering 171 services'.
problem: Conflicting figure not reported. The RCC says the same plan sets out '162 additional online services', and this item is listed in reform_items.
suggested_fix: Give both figures and say that they are not reconciled.

claim: 'A new eUprava portal was launched in December 2024'.
problem: Conflict not reported. The monitor says the government adopted an information note on establishing the portal in December 2024 and 'the new portal was not functional'. The Commission and the event report say launched. The item is listed in implementation_items but the conflict is not stated.
suggested_fix: Record that launch dates differ in kind: decision in December 2024, first services in April 2025.

claim: 'Montenegro's 2023 cybersecurity crisis'.
problem: Date conflict not reported. The Commission says 2023; the government's action plan says 'after the 2022 attacks'.
suggested_fix: Attribute the date to the Commission and note the government's different date.

claim: The Commission's 'no noticeable improvement' as of the end of 2023.
problem: Quoted accurately, but the item is not in any item list in the case.
suggested_fix: Add it to implementation_items or outcome_items.

case_or_judgement: CMP-0009; success INT-MNE-0022>MNE-CSO-2025-001-0019; INT-MNE-0020; INT-MNE-0021; INT-MNE-0022
claim: 'the independent monitor'; 'An independent monitor states the result'.
problem: Overstated. Source quality marks independence 'partly', because the monitored ministry co-funds the project (SQ-00180), and the event report says the same. For Albania the monitor is also 'partly' (SQ-00144) and names the implementing agency as a partner, while INT-ALB-0002 and the worked row call it independent.
suggested_fix: Say 'non-government monitor, co-funded by the ministry' for Montenegro, and adjust the Albanian wording to match SQ-00144.

claim: worked: 'It should be counted once with the report's finding.'
problem: A second worked row on the same claim from the same organisation counts it twice in any tally, and the event report is rated Low (SQ-00182). The monitor's own sentence also carries the caveat that data on services were still being collected.
suggested_fix: Merge with the row on item 0019, or mark this row as corroboration only, without its own success value.

claim: 'an official's slower than expected'.
problem: Refers to another matter. The official's sentence concerns the single-entry principle in the plan (pass 2 note), not delivery of the 57 services.
suggested_fix: Say what the remark concerns, or remove it from the delivery conflict.

claim: Status rests on the 1,070 transactions item.
problem: The item is classified out_of_scope in pass 2 and has no link to RI-TEC-036 (LIM-0026). The row sits in the issue's judgement file without saying so.
suggested_fix: Note the classification in the reason, as the INT-MDA-0015 row does for its issue, or move the row out.

claim: 'The RCC names the strategy as adopted'.
problem: Not supported. The item says the digital strategy 'complements' the Public Administration Reform Strategy 2022-2026 and does not say adopted.
suggested_fix: Say that the RCC refers to the strategy as existing; find an item on adoption, or use unclear.

claim: insufficient_evidence: 'It does not establish the status of the Agenda itself on this measure.'
problem: True of the cited item, but the monitor's text (page 33) says one reform in the Reform Agenda is user-friendly digital public services, starting with the Digital Services Plan 2025-2027, and this has not been extracted.
suggested_fix: Extract the passage and reconsider the value.

claim: conditional; 'fits North Macedonia's unfilled posts and fragmented ownership'.
problem: The item is a conclusion about Montenegro, typed as a lesson by the rule default, and does not state a lesson for others. The cited North Macedonian items support capacity and ownership, not 'political will', which is half of the claim. The speaker conflict with item 0016 is correctly flagged; the source text shows it is the report's closing line, not Polović's.
suggested_fix: Limit the transfer to capacity, or propose insufficient_evidence on political will. Correct the speaker on 0016 at the gate.

claim: 'on condition that user involvement is in design, as North Macedonia's Reform Agenda plans for user experience'.
problem: The cited item does not support this. It prioritises user experience design and usability, and it says nothing about consulting direct beneficiaries, which is the lesson in the Moldovan item.
suggested_fix: Remove the implied match, or say that the Reform Agenda covers usability but not user involvement, which makes the condition unmet at present.
